prompt: Summarize this scientific methods section into a single paragraph a journalist could use, explicitly flagging any part of the methodology that limits how strongly the results can be generalized: 'Participants (n=45, convenience sample from a single university) completed a 6-week intervention involving daily 10-minute mindfulness sessions via a mobile app. Self-reported stress levels were measured using the PSS-10 scale at baseline and post-intervention. No control group was used due to resource constraints; instead, a within-subjects pre-post design was employed.'

response_text: The study recruited 45 volunteers from a single university (a convenience sample) to complete a six‑week, daily 10‑minute mindfulness program delivered via a mobile app, with participants rating their own stress using the 10‑item Perceived Stress Scale (PSS‑10) before and after the intervention; however, because the researchers did not include a control group—citing resource constraints—and relied on self‑report measures in a relatively small, homogeneous sample, the ability to generalize the findings to broader populations or to attribute stress reductions specifically to the mindfulness app is limited.
